title: SimHash multiplex coalescer and GPU slab relocation for fuzzy prompt dedupe
creator: Ava Chen
description: Investigate and implement a fuzzy deduplication layer for prefix/prompt KV caching that uses SimHash-based signatures to merge semantically similar prefixes across requests, combined with a two-phase GPU slab relocation strategy to reduce fragmentation and overall KV memory footprint without regressing tail latency.
background: Current prefix caching is strictly content-addressed: identical token sequences get deduped, but paraphrases or template variants with small differences miss the cache. This leads to wasted GPU-resident KV memory and lower effective hit rates for interactive workloads. Additionally, frequent small evictions and insertions cause slab fragmentation on the GPU, raising the resident working set and harming throughput under memory pressure.
proposal: Add a lightweight similarity-signature pipeline at batching ingress that computes a SimHash (64-bit) over normalized token sequences and prompt metadata. At insert time, the coalescer probes a per-shard L2 table (content + simhash buckets) to find near-matches within Hamming radius <= 3. Matches above a confidence threshold are soft-merged: the request reuses the matched KV entries but records a short-lived alias mapping. To keep GPU memory compact, implement a two-phase slab relocation background worker: phase 1 marks low-usage fragments for relocation and assigns eviction credits; phase 2 streams selected fragments to new contiguous slab regions using GPU-to-GPU or pinned host staging to avoid blocking front-line inference. The system exposes runtime knobs: simhash_threshold, alias_ttl, relocation_batch_size, and compaction_window_ms.
design_decisions: Use SimHash because it provides an inexpensive, locality-preserving binary signature that we can compute on the tokenized prefix with fast bit ops. We opted for soft-aliasing rather than in-place rewriting to avoid invalidating in-flight KV pointers. Two-phase relocation separates decisioning from copy to bound tail latency during compaction. We keep the data structure per tenant-shard to preserve isolation and to allow tenant-specific thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Improve effective KV hit rate for interactive chat workloads by >= 12% (measured across 3 representative customer workloads),
Reduce GPU-resident KV fragmentation overhead (wasted bytes due to free gaps) by >= 18% in steady state,
End-to-end p50/p95 generation latency change <= +5% / +10% respectively compared to baseline when coalescing enabled,
No correctness regressions: sequence reconstruction for reused KV must produce identical tokens for callers that depend on cache reuse; aliasing metadata includes provenance and confidence,
Feature gated and controllable per-customer; safe default off for Dedicated/Private customers until vetted.
implementation_plan: Phase A: Instrumentation and simhash pipeline (compute, store, and probe) behind feature flag (2 weeks),
Phase B: Soft-alias maps and alias-aware KV lookup with TTL/metrics (2 weeks),
Phase C: GPU slab relocation worker prototype on staging with small-scale compaction (2 weeks),
Phase D: Integrate relocation with request path safeguards and run long soak tests on Dedicated clusters (3 weeks),
Phase E: Rollout: internal canary -> 10% hosted -> 50% -> global, with rollback on regression signals (2 weeks)
milestones: Slab relocation worker merged to staging (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1726),
Canary metrics meet acceptance criteria and safe for gradual rollout
metrics_and_observability: simhash_hit_rate: fraction of lookups that returned a soft-merged alias
kv_effective_hit_rate: baseline-eq hit rate including soft-merges
gpu_fragmentation_bytes: bytes in free gaps inside allocated slabs
relocation_io_bytes: data moved by compaction worker per minute
latency_p50_p95: model generation latencies with coalescer on/off
alias_confidence_histogram: distribution of simhash hamming distances used for merges
risks: False merges: semantically different prefixes could be merged if simhash collisions occur; mitigations include conservative thresholding and storing provenance fingerprints,
Increased CPU overhead at ingress for signature computation under very high QPS; mitigation: SIMD-optimized simhash and sample-based probing,
Relocation IO can contend with inference DMA on shared PCIe links if not rate-limited,
Complexity of per-tenant thresholds increases operational surface—must expose safe defaults and telemetry
rollback_plan: Feature flag: rollback by disabling simhash coalescer and alias read path. If relocation causes regressions, pause worker and schedule immediate freeze of relocation tasks; existing aliases are time-limited so disabling coalescer naturally decays behavior.
test_plan: Unit tests for simhash computation and Hamming radius probe logic,
Integration test: synthetic workload with paraphrased templates to verify improved reuse,
Performance test: throughput and tail latency with relocation worker active under sustained load,
Chaos: kill relocation worker during active compaction and assert safety invariants (no corrupt KV entries)
